newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bond prices slip ahead of German, U.S data.
newsitem.headline: Danish bond prices slip ahead of German, U.S data.

text.p: Danish bond prices continued to fall on Thursday, with the market anxiously awaiting German budget forecasts and their implications for EMU, as well as key U.S. indicators due this afternoon.

At 1130 GMT the benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was down 0.25 point from Wednesday's close, at 111.37, yielding 6.27 percent. The forthcoming benchmark seven percent state bond due 2007 was down 0.30 to 103.95, yielding 6.46 percent.
The yield gap between the 2006 bond and the German bund was unchanged from its earlier 56 basis points and the 2007-bund gap was likewise static at 74 bp.
The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 fell 0.10 point, to 89.90.
The crown firmed to 3.8082 per mark, from Wednesday's 3.8067. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
